title: Personal experiences bridge moral and political divides better than facts
byline: Kubin E.; Puryear C.; Schein C.; Gray K.
design_rationale: Studies 4 and 6–10 compare written accounts of political opponents’ personal experiences with factual justifications before rationality, respect, and interaction ratings; other studies use field or archival methods.
retrieval_diagnosis: The indexed abstract emphasizes survey studies and mixed methods, without describing the requested nearby reading/manipulation terms; experimental structure becomes clear in the full text.
parser_note: A qualifying text-vignette subset is present, but article-level pooling with conversations or archival studies and the original questionnaire must be checked.
evidence_location: PDF pp. 3–5; US population statement p. 7

title: Algorithmic Discrimination Causes Less Moral Outrage Than Human Discrimination
byline: Bigman Y.E.; Wilson D.; Arnestad M.N.; Waytz A.; Gray K.
design_rationale: Participants receive randomized descriptions of discriminatory hiring by a human or algorithm and report prejudice, outrage, and company responsibility; the paper includes US, UK, Canadian, and Norwegian samples.
retrieval_diagnosis: The abstract describes eight studies and online samples but does not state the required nearby reading/manipulation procedure; broad study terminology also weakens an experiment-token gate.
parser_note: Written between-group scenarios are eligible; multiple studies, repeated ratings, and questionnaire layout still require parser validation.

title: Equating silence with violence: When White Americans feel threatened by anti-racist messages
byline: Kachanoff F.J.; Kteily N.; Gray K.
design_rationale: White US respondents are randomized to versions of an anti-racist graphic with different wording and then report threat and message resistance; later studies vary message exposure and phrasing.
retrieval_diagnosis: This is the newly retrieved Gray article: the abstract places manipulating near messages and explicitly describes experimental variation, satisfying the proposed proximity clause.
parser_note: The treatment combines written language and a graphic; recovery of stimulus images and the questionnaire needs checking before parser use.

title: Threat Rejection Fuels Political Dehumanization
byline: Kubin E.; Kachanoff F.J.; Gray K.
design_rationale: In Studies 3a and 3b, US respondents receive randomized rationales for an opponent’s social-distancing position and then report condemnation and dehumanization; earlier studies are observational.
retrieval_diagnosis: The abstract describes multiple studies and a threat-acknowledgment intervention without the requested reading/manipulation phrasing; its summary does not label the work as experiments.
parser_note: Eligible fixed text conditions exist, but branching to an opposing position and separation from observational studies require questionnaire-level verification.

title: Identity concerns drive belief: The impact of partisan identity on the belief and dissemination of true and false news
byline: Pereira A.; Harris E.; Van Bavel J.J.
design_rationale: US partisans read politician quotations or fabricated news whose partisan source and content are experimentally varied, then rate belief and willingness to share.
retrieval_diagnosis: This is the newly retrieved Van Bavel article: its abstract directly connects reading with news and explicitly reports three experiments.
parser_note: Repeated stimulus ratings and source/content conditions require questionnaire and data-format checks; focal author is last.

title: Allocating moral responsibility to multiple agents
byline: Gantman A.P.; Sternisko A.; Gollwitzer P.M.; Oettingen G.; Van Bavel J.J.
design_rationale: Online respondents read altered company-action scenarios and rate blame, intention, punishment, or praise; randomized scenario versions and harm/help conditions provide eligible content manipulations.
retrieval_diagnosis: The abstract describes participants learning about an oil spill and judging responsibility; that wording omits the proposed reading or manipulation proximity terms although full methods explicitly describe reading scenarios.
parser_note: Multiple-agent judgments and a fixed-sum blame question need parser checks; Mechanical Turk alone does not establish sample country.

title: The Role of Political Devotion in Sharing Partisan Misinformation and Resistance to Fact-Checking
byline: Pretus C.; Servin-Barthet C.; Harris E.A.; Brady W.J.; Vilarroya O.; Van Bavel J.J.
design_rationale: Online samples in Spain and the US rate sharing likelihood for researcher-created posts under different fact-check or accuracy-prompt conditions; a separate Spanish neuroimaging study also appears.
retrieval_diagnosis: The abstract reports experiments, misinformation, and nudges, but lacks the required nearby reading/manipulation language; those procedures are described in the full text.
parser_note: The online subset is eligible, but repeated blocks and fact-check variants require questionnaire verification; the neuroimaging component should not be treated as a simple survey dataset.

title: Accuracy and social motivations shape judgements of (mis)information
byline: Rathje S.; Roozenbeek J.; Van Bavel J.J.; van der Linden S.
design_rationale: US online respondents receive accuracy incentives or a brief accuracy-motivation text before judging headline truth; source cues and incentive conditions are experimentally varied.
retrieval_diagnosis: The broader previous candidate query already retrieves this article. The new clause misses its abstract, which describes incentives and headlines without the specified nearby reading/manipulation terms; Van Bavel is third of four authors and receives no first/last credit.
parser_note: Repeated headlines and incentive conditions require questionnaire-level parsing checks; middle authorship remains distinct from eligibility.
